common.metaDescription: Remote management for a Dainty Lass server

login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Server management

errors.discord_failed: Discord sign-in did not finish. Try again in a moment.
errors.twitch_failed: Twitch sign-in did not finish. Try again in a moment.
errors.passkey_failed: That passkey did not work. Add one from your account page after signing in another way.
errors.email_failed: The code could not be sent. Check the address and try again.
errors.code_invalid: That code is wrong or has expired. Ask for a new one.
errors.rate_limited: Too many tries. Wait a minute, then try again.
errors.dev_failed: Development sign-in failed. Check the server log.
errors.unknown: Sign-in did not finish. Try again.

login.or: or get a code by email
login.codeSent: We sent a 6-digit code to {email}. It works once, for five minutes.
login.anyone: Anyone can sign in. What you see depends on your role on this server.

overview.subtitle: {name}, a {mode} server
overview.subtitleOffline: The game server is not answering

overview.chatActivityLabel: {total} messages in the last 24 hours, {flagged} flagged
overview.huntsUnavailable: Hunts are unavailable while the game server is not answering.
overview.changesToday: {count, plural, =0 {No changes today} one {# change today} other {# changes today}}

audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Every change made from this dashboard, with what it replaced
audit.count: {count, plural, =0 {No changes} one {# change} other {# changes}}
audit.confirmBody: {change}. Undoing it puts back what it replaced, and is recorded as a change of its own.

actions.controller_repair: {actor} issued a new pairing code for {target}
actions.member_role_added: {actor} was given the approved Discord role
actions.member_role_failed: The approved Discord role could not be given to {actor}
actions.chat_filter_flagged: The chat filter flagged a line from {target}
actions.chat_filter_masked: The chat filter masked a line from {target}
actions.chat_filter_blocked: The chat filter blocked a line from {target}

audit.openChatLine: Open this line in the chat log

players.title: Players
players.description: Every account on the server, from the backend's admin routes
players.fromChatLog: The backend is not answering, so this list comes from the chat log: everyone who has spoken, newest first.
players.noneKnown: No players have spoken in chat yet.
players.protected: This account holds the backend's admin role, so kicks, timeouts and bans are refused for it.
players.partialData: Showing what the dashboard and the backend know; live status and moderation return when the game server answers.
players.noChat: This player has not said anything the dashboard has received.
players.allChat: Open the full chat log for this player
players.noHistory: No staff actions on this player yet.
players.accessExplain: The backend's own account state: separate from game bans, it decides whether the launcher may sign in at all.
players.roleTesterExplain: Unlocks the backend's tester tools for this account.

moderation.customPlaceholder: The player reads this in the launcher
moderation.kickOffline: Only an online player can be kicked
moderation.banWarning: A ban lasts until someone lifts it. The player's running game stops at its next request.

explain.kick: Closes their chat connections and signs them out. They are not banned and may come straight back.
explain.timeout: Bans them until the time runs out, then lifts it automatically.
explain.ban: Bans them until someone lifts it. They read the reason in the launcher.
explain.unban: Lifts a ban or a timeout, so they can play again.

moderation.banEverywhereHint: Every controller that can be reached and has an account with this name bans it. Each ban is recorded and can be undone on its own.
moderation.fleetDone: {done, plural, =0 {Banned on no controller} one {Banned on # controller} other {Banned on # controllers}} of {total}.{absent, plural, =0 {} one { # has no such account.} other { # have no such account.}}{missed, plural, =0 {} one { # could not be reached or refused:} other { # could not be reached or refused:}}

reports.title: Reports
reports.description: Player reports from the game, Discord and staff, oldest first
reports.emptyQueueHint: New reports from the game and Discord land here.
reports.prior: {count, plural, one {# earlier report} other {# earlier reports}}
reports.contextHint: {minutes} minutes either side of the reported moment.
reports.noContext: No chat from around that time.
reports.noRelated: No other reports against this player.
reports.noNotes: No notes yet. Notes are visible to staff only.
reports.notePlaceholder: What you checked, who you spoke to…
reports.resolutionShown: Also the reason the player reads in the launcher.

chat.title: Chat logs
chat.description: City, party and guild chat as the backend relays it. Direct messages are read from a player's page, with a reason, and each read is audited.

filter.title: Chat filter
filter.description: {count, plural, =0 {No terms} one {# term} other {# terms}}, revision {version}
filter.deleteBody: "{pattern}" stops being filtered. The change can be undone from the revisions below.
filter.testerHint: See what the current list would do, without sending anything.
filter.samplePlaceholder: Type a message as a player would

actionHelp.flag: Delivered as sent, and marked in the log for review.
actionHelp.mask: Delivered with the matched part replaced by asterisks.
actionHelp.block: Not delivered. The sender sees it as sent.

filter.enforcement: The backend fetches this list and enforces it; the dashboard rates lines on arrival with the same rules.
filter.emptyHint: Add a term to start masking or flagging chat.

kindHelp.word: Matches the word on its own, ignoring case, spacing tricks and look-alikes such as 0 for o.
kindHelp.substring: Matches inside other words too, with the same look-alike handling.
kindHelp.regex: A JavaScript regular expression, matched case-insensitively.

filter.historyHint: Every change saves the whole list as a new revision. Restoring one makes it current again.

revisions.empty: No revisions yet: the first change records where it started from.
revisions.confirmBody: Its state becomes current, saved as a new version. Nothing newer is deleted, so this can be undone too.

staff.title: Members
staff.description: Everyone who has signed in, and what each may see
staff.addExplain: Sets their role before they first sign in with Discord. Nothing is sent to them.
staff.discordIdHint: In Discord, turn on Developer Mode, then right-click the person and Copy User ID.
staff.discordIdInvalid: A Discord id is 17 to 20 digits
staff.guildSyncHint: Members who follow Discord roles are re-checked at every sign-in. Changing someone's role here pins it until you set them to follow Discord again.

roleHelp.owner: Everything, including settings and other owners
roleHelp.admin: Everything a moderator sees, plus the audit log, undo, accounts, the chat filter and members
roleHelp.moderator: Reports, chat logs, kicks, timeouts and bans
roleHelp.user: The overview, players and controllers; no reports, chat or audit log

staff.historyHint: Roles and access as they were. Restoring never deletes anyone; people added since are disabled.
staff.followDiscordHint: Take the role from their Discord roles at their next sign-in

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Each save is a revision you can restore below.
settings.serverNameHint: Shown on the sign-in page and in browser tabs.
settings.discordHint: Optionally let roles in your Discord server set each member's tier, instead of setting it on the Members page.
settings.guildIdHint: Leave empty and everyone signs in as a user until an admin raises them.
settings.reasonsHint: One per line. Offered when timing out, banning or changing access.
settings.contextMinutesHint: Minutes of chat shown either side of a reported moment.
settings.retentionHint: Chat older than this is deleted every hour as new chat arrives, or now with Prune.
settings.pruned: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to prune} one {# message deleted} other {# messages deleted}}
settings.connectionsHint: Set in the dashboard's environment, not here. Secrets are never shown.
settings.historyHint: Every save of these settings, newest first.
settings.approvedRoleIdHint: Holding it counts as approved; accepting the terms adds it, with the bot below.
settings.onboardingHint: What someone new sees before the dashboard.
settings.requireApproval: Ask newcomers to accept the terms
settings.requireApprovalHint: Users who are not approved see a welcome page first. Moderators and above never do.
settings.tosHint: Markdown. Currently version {version}; saving a change makes a new version, and everyone who was approved by accepting the terms is asked again.
settings.botMissing: DASHBOARD_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN is not set, so accepting the terms cannot add the approved role in Discord.

errors.unauthenticated: Your session ended. Sign in again.
errors.invalid_input: Check the highlighted values and try again.
errors.conflict: That already exists, or changed while you were looking at it.
errors.reason_required: Give a reason of 3 to 400 characters.
errors.self_lockout: You cannot remove your own access.
errors.last_owner: The server needs at least one enabled owner.
errors.not_revertible: This change cannot be undone automatically.
errors.already_reverted: This change has already been undone.
errors.regex_invalid: That is not a valid regular expression.
errors.game_unavailable: The game server is not answering.
errors.game_not_configured: The dashboard is not connected to the game server ({detail} is unset).
errors.protected_account: Accounts with the backend's admin role cannot be moderated.
errors.already_banned: That player is already banned; lift the ban first.
errors.not_timed_out: That player is not timed out.
errors.unknown: Something went wrong. The server log has the details.
errors.controller_offline: {detail} is not connected. Its agent may be stopped or its host offline.
errors.game_timeout: The controller took too long to answer.
errors.forbidden_call: The agent refused a call it does not allow ({detail}).
errors.last_sign_in: That is your only way to sign in. Add another first.

fleet.title: Controllers
fleet.description: The hosts running game servers. Each one other than this dashboard's runs an agent that connects here.
fleet.downCount: {count, plural, one {# not answering} other {# not answering}}
fleet.downBanner: {count, plural, one {# controller is not answering} other {# controllers are not answering}}
fleet.playersOverTimeLabel: Players online over the last 24 hours
fleet.weekLabel: Players online over the last week
fleet.huntCount: {count, plural, =0 {None running} one {# running} other {# running}}
fleet.playersAcross: {count, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}} across the fleet
fleet.someUnanswered: {count, plural, one {# controller did not answer} other {# controllers did not answer}}
fleet.name: Name
fleet.addExplain: You get a one-time code to start its agent with. Nothing on that host needs a port opened.
fleet.localDescription: The controller this dashboard runs on
fleet.removeBody: Its agent is disconnected and its token stops working. Chat, reports and history from it stay, labelled with its id.
fleet.pendingHint: Start the agent on that host with the pairing code. Re-pair from Actions if the code expired.
fleet.localNotConfigured: This host's admin API key is not set, so the dashboard cannot reach its game server (DASHBOARD_ADMIN_API_KEY).

pairing.title: Pair {name}
pairing.step1: On that host, write these into an env file. The two secrets come from its own secrets.env and never leave it.
pairing.step2: Then start the agent from a dainty-dash checkout:
pairing.after: The code works once. The agent stores the token it gets in exchange and reconnects with it from then on.
pairing.insecure: This dashboard's address is not HTTPS. Agents send their token with every request, so put the dashboard behind TLS before pairing hosts over the internet.

logs.title: Logs
logs.hint: How this server's console log reads, and the Graylog (GELF) collector it ships every line to. Saved to its settings.toml; the server takes it at its next start.
logs.unavailable: This controller did not answer for its log settings. It may be offline, or running an older server.
logs.restartNeeded: Saved. Restart the server for these settings to take effect.
logs.gelfUrlHint: https:// anywhere; http:// or tcp://host:port only to the server's own machine or a private network. Empty stops shipping.

account.title: Your account
account.description: How you sign in. There are no passwords: use Discord, Twitch, a passkey or a code by email.
account.signInsHint: Link more than one, so losing one does not lock you out. Discord also lets the server's roles set what you can see.
account.noEmail: No address yet. Signing in with Discord or Twitch adds one.
account.lastWay: Your only way to sign in. Add another first.
account.passkeysHint: A passkey signs you in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN. It is stored by your device or password manager and never leaves it.
account.passkeyNameHint: So you can tell them apart, like "Work laptop".
account.failed: That did not work. Try again.
account.linkFailed: Linking did not finish. That account may already belong to someone else here.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.heading: Welcome to {server}
welcome.subtitle: Set up your account and accept the server terms to continue.
welcome.subtitleRenew: Read the new terms and accept them to continue.
welcome.accountHint: Shown to staff in place of your sign-in name.
welcome.displayNameInvalid: Use 2 to 32 letters, numbers, spaces and . _ ' -
welcome.gameNameHint: If you play here, so staff can find you.
welcome.gameNameInvalid: In-game names are 3 to 16 letters, numbers and _
welcome.noTerms: This server has not written its terms yet.
welcome.accept: I have read and accept the {server} terms
welcome.roleHint: If your Discord is linked, accepting also gives you the server's member role there.
welcome.roleNotAdded: You're in, but the Discord role could not be added. Ask a moderator.
welcome.termsChanged: The terms changed while you were reading. Read the new version.

signInCode.subject: {code} is your {server} sign-in code
signInCode.body:
Your {server} dashboard sign-in code is {code}.

It works once, for five minutes. If you did not ask for it, ignore this email.

performance.title: Performance
performance.noneHint: The admin service's /metrics has not answered. It needs a Dainty Lass server that serves metrics and the admin key; another controller also needs an agent recent enough to report them.
performance.requestsLabel: Requests per minute over the last hour, with server errors in red
performance.cpuLabel: CPU use over the last hour, in percent of one core
performance.memoryLabel: Resident memory over the last hour
performance.componentsHint: CPU and memory where a process has the component's name; the rest run inside the controller.
performance.directorDown: The Director is not answering, so no game servers are listed.
performance.processesHint: The controller and every process it started. Metrics do not say which process runs which game server.
performance.noChat: No chat lines in this window.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.hint: Only in this browser. Applied as you pick.

direct.title: {name}'s direct messages
direct.explain: Direct messages are private, so they stay out of the chat logs and exports. Reading them records who read them, whose they were and why in the audit log, where admins see it.
direct.reason: Why you need to read them
direct.recorded: This read is in the audit log
direct.none: {name} has no direct messages the dashboard has received.

games.title: Game servers
games.freeHunts: {count, plural, one {# free hunt slot} other {# free hunt slots}}
games.waiting: Waiting for the server's first report
games.unreachable: The admin API didn't answer, so the game servers are unknown

installs.title: Installs
installs.hint: Every server the remote controller beside this dashboard manages, from its last report
installs.notController: This server isn't a remote controller, so there are no installs to list

signup.title: Account creation
signup.hint: Whether people may create an account themselves. While it's on, the Discord bot's /key sends this page; otherwise it sends a single-use login invite.
signup.enabledHint: Anyone can read whether this is on, and the page below, at /api/public/signup.
signup.urlHint: An http or https address, without a username or password in it.
signup.urlMissing: Account creation is on but has no page, so /key keeps sending login invites.

grants.title: Grant to {name}
grants.explain: Items, currencies and levels go through the game's own grant path, as if the game had given them.
grants.itemPlaceholder: Search catalog ids, such as a weapon or armour id
grants.trackPlaceholder: Pick a level or pass track
grants.whenOnline: The player is online: the game shows it after their next inventory load, when they travel or sign in again.
grants.whenOffline: The player sees it the next time they sign in.
grants.partialTitle: Granted in part: see what failed below

result.items: {count, plural, one {# item or currency stack} other {# item or currency stacks}}

crashReports.title: Crash reports
crashReports.description: Game crashes players sent from the launcher. The full files stay on the game server.
crashReports.emptyHint: When a player sends a crash report from the launcher, it shows here.
crashReports.noText: Not sent as text. Read it on the game server.
